---
id: "smk-09"
title: "Common raven"
---

The common raven is a large, all-black member of the crow family found across the Northern Hemisphere, from Arctic tundra to deserts and mountains. It is among the largest of the songbirds, with a wingspan of up to 1.5 metres, a heavy bill and a wedge-shaped tail that distinguishes it from crows in flight. Ravens are omnivorous scavengers that eat carrion, insects, grain, berries, small animals and food waste, and they are known for their intelligence: they solve problems, use tools in experiments, remember individual people and play in the air. Pairs mate for life and build large stick nests on cliffs or in tall trees. The raven has a deep, croaking call and a wide repertoire of other sounds. It features prominently in the mythology of many cultures, from Norse legends of Odin's ravens to the stories of the peoples of the Pacific Northwest.
